claim: A complete scripted ZFS health check on Linux can be built from zpool list -H -o name/health/cap/frag plus zpool status parsing, with concrete thresholds: state != ONLINE is CRITICAL, capacity > 85% WARNING, fragmentation > 50% WARNING, any per-device CKSUM > 0 WARNING, and errors line != 'No known data errors' WARNING.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent ZFS sensor thresholds have a concrete, published practitioner baseline to adopt or adapt
scope_conditions: Ubuntu/Linux ZFS (zpool CLI); blog guide technically validated May 2026

claim: Recommended ZFS alert bands from the guide: capacity alert above 80% and critical above 90%; fragmentation monitor above 30% and address above 50%; ARC hit ratio below 80% flags RAM constraints; any scrub errors or non-zero CKSUM warrants investigation.
stance_target: two-tier (warning/critical) ZFS threshold bands for agent sensor configuration
quoted_support:
Pool health - should always be ONLINE
Capacity - alert above 80%, critical above 90%
Fragmentation - monitor above 30%, address above 50%
CKSUM errors - any non-zero value warrants investigation
ARC hit ratio - below 80% may indicate RAM constraints

claim: ZFS on Linux ships zed (ZFS Event Daemon, package zfs-zed, service zfs-zed.service) which emits email alerts on pool state changes, scrub completion, resilver completion, and device errors — an event-driven channel complementing polling.
stance_target: the agent can either consume zed events or replicate its triggers; event-driven ZFS alerting is built into the platform on Linux
quoted_support: ZFS includes zed, the ZFS Event Daemon, which monitors ZFS events and can send email alerts ... zed sends emails on pool state changes, scrub completion, resilver completion, and device errors.

claim: prometheus-node-exporter on Linux exposes ZFS metrics (node_zfs_arc_size, node_zfs_arc_hits/misses, node_zfs_zpool_nread, node_zfs_zpool_nwritten labelled per zpool) on port 9100, and ARC statistics are readable from /proc/spl/kstat/zfs/arcstats.
stance_target: alternative agent-side ZFS telemetry path: either the agent reads /proc/spl/kstat/zfs directly or reuses node-exporter metric names for ecosystem compatibility
scope_conditions: Ubuntu with prometheus-node-exporter; ZFS ARC stats via /proc/spl/kstat/zfs/arcstats

claim: CKSUM errors in ZFS can be transient in small numbers, but repeated or growing CKSUM errors indicate a failing disk, bad SATA/SAS cable, or controller issue — i.e. error-count trend, not just presence, is the diagnostic signal.
stance_target: agent ZFS alerting should track error-counter deltas over time (rate of growth), not just absolute values
quoted_support: Even a few CKSUM errors without corresponding disk errors can be transient. Repeated or growing CKSUM errors indicate a failing disk, bad SATA/SAS cable, or controller issue.

claim: 'zpool list -H -o name,health,cap,frag' gives scriptable single-line-per-pool output for health/capacity/fragmentation, and 'zpool iostat -ql' exposes per-op latency percentiles to identify slow disks.
stance_target: the agent's ZFS collector has documented low-friction CLI surfaces for pool health and disk latency without parsing verbose human output
quoted_support:
sudo zpool iostat -ql 5
This shows operation latency which helps identify slow disks.

claim: Excessively long resilver durations indicate slow or stressed disks, and scrub outputs with any errors warrant alerting — resilience-operation telemetry belongs in fleet monitoring alongside pool state.
stance_target: agent should alert on resilver/scrub anomalies, not just on pool state changes
quoted_support: Resilver duration - excessively long resilvers indicate slow/stressed disks
